text:
acme-eng: Hey, we started seeing connection failures to our private VPC endpoints after the cert rotation last night. OpenVPN clients and the internal HAProxy frontends both report TLS verify errors. No config changes on our side.

julie-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the client error and a server-side TLS log?

acme-eng: Client error: 'TLS: alert number 20' then 'certificate verify failed'. Server (haproxy) shows: 'SSL handshake failure, no certificate found' for a bunch of clients.

sam-devops: Can you run these and paste outputs?
```
openssl s_client -connect private-vpc.example.com:443 -showcerts
openssl verify -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-chain.pem /etc/ssl/private/rotated.pem
cat -A /etc/ssl/private/rotated.pem | sed -n '1,120p'
```

acme-eng: Running now, output clipped but notably openssl verify fails: 'unable to get local issuer certificate'. s_client prints the server cert and then 'verify return:1' but clients still fail. cat -A shows an odd line: the uploaded bundle ends with "-----END CERTIFICATE-----$" and an extra blank line with only CRLF characters (shown as '^M$' with cat -A).

kevin-platform: That could be the issue — some parsers choke on extra trailing CRLF or stray newline before EOF, especially if the rotation script concatenated files with an extra echo. Can you paste exact s_client full output?

acme-eng: Full s_client excerpt:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = ExampleRoot, CN = Example Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=private-vpc.example.com
   i:/CN=intermediate.example.com
 1 s:/CN=intermediate.example.com
   i:/CN=Example Root CA
---
Server certificate
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF....(omitted)....
-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n
---
SSL handshake has read 3456 bytes and written 562 bytes
---
```
Note the explicit '\n' printed after END CERTIFICATE in the s_client dump.

sam-devops: Hmm. Also check that the uploaded bundle has the intermediate in the correct order: server cert first, then intermediate(s), then root (optional). If there's an extra newline or stray characters between certs haproxy/openssl on older builds sometimes treat the file as truncated and skip the chain.

julie-support: Do you also have any OCSP stapling enabled? We had reports where an OCSP timeout made clients fail if they insist on fresh revocation checks and the host cannot reach the responder due to egress allowlist.

acme-eng: Yes, we enable stapling. For the same time window our firewall logs show outbound to ocsp.responder.example.org being denied — customer infra team tightened egress rules overnight.

kevin-platform: That's two plausible contributors: malformed bundle AND blocked OCSP. Small stack: client fails to verify because HAProxy didn't present chain due to parse error, and OCSP timeouts aggravated failures for clients that do revocation checks.

sam-devops: Short remediation steps we recommend now:
1) Re-upload a sanitized PEM bundle where each cert ends exactly with a single LF and no extra CR or blank lines. Use this to validate locally first:
```
awk 'BEGINFILE{first=1} /-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----/{if(!first)print ""; first=0} {print}' rotated.pem > rotated.fixed.pem
openssl verify -CAfile <(awk '/*BEGIN CERT/{print; while(getline && /END CERT/) {print; if(/END CERTIFICATE/) break}}' rotated.fixed.pem) rotated.fixed.pem || true
```
2) Temporarily allow egress to OCSP responder (or disable stapling while fixing bundle) so clients don't fail due to timeouts.
3) Roll back to previous cert if immediate connectivity must be restored.
4) Add an incoming validation step in the rotator to strip trailing whitespace and verify chain order, reject upload with actionable error.

acme-eng: We did step 1 locally and confirmed rotated.fixed.pem loads cleanly with openssl verify and haproxy started presenting the chain. Rolling to prod now.

ops-bot: [deploy] rolling restart of haproxy-proxy/region-a (canary -> stable) started by sam-devops at 2026-03-17T02:10:12Z

julie-support: Great — after the restart can you confirm OpenVPN clients can reconnect? Also, can you paste the fixed file diff? We want a short audit trail for support.

acme-eng: Clients reconnected after restart and allowing OCSP traffic. Diff was basically the rotator had appended an extra '\r\n' between the last cert and EOF; removing it fixed parse. Updated rotator script PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/rotator/pulls/452 (validation + trim).

kevin-platform: Followups we'll do on our side:
- Add server-side validation in the control plane that rejects PEM uploads with trailing blank lines or non-PEM junk.
- Add a check in the private deployment guide about egress allowlist for OCSP responders and common CRL/OCSP hosts.
- Add an alert rule: if >5% TLS handshakes fail with 'no certificate presented' after rotation event, auto-fail rotation and notify on-call.

sam-devops: I have opened infra/rotator#452 and will push a hotfix to trim and validate bundles; target patch today.

julie-support: Marking as resolved for now since client connectivity restored. acme-eng please ping if you see recurrence and we'll escalate to on-call. :thumbsup:"
